scientific_name: Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri (syn. Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri)
description: Citrus canker is a highly contagious bacterial disease affecting citrus plants. It causes lesions on leaves, stems, and fruits, leading to premature leaf and fruit drop and reduced fruit quality. Although infected fruits are edible, they are not marketable due to their appearance.
symptoms_and_damage: Small raised blister-like lesions with water-soaked margins
Yellow halos surrounding lesions on leaves and fruits
Necrotic spots on leaves, stems, and fruits
disease_cycle_and_spread: Bacteria survive in lesions on leaves, stems, and fruits
Spread through wind-driven rain and water splash
Long-distance spread occurs mainly through movement of infected plant material
Insects, birds, and animals may contribute to local spread
Leafminer damage increases infection by creating wounds
favorable_conditions: Presence of free water on plant surfaces
pathogen_characteristics: Produces yellow pigment called xanthomonadin in culture
monitoring: Inspect leaves for raised lesions with yellow halos
Check fruits for corky or cracked lesions
Observe twig lesions that may serve as infection sources
management: Apply copper-based sprays as preventive treatment
Install windbreaks to reduce spread by wind-driven rain
Disinfect tools, equipment, and clothing when entering or leaving orchards
Remove infected trees in areas where the disease is not yet established
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension – Citrus Research and Education Center, Lake Alfred, Florida
